input.question: If matter attracts matter (gravity), does anti-matter repel matter (anti-matter)?
input.ground_truth: Gravity is a response to mass, it doesn't care what kind of matter has the mass. Both matter and antimatter have mass, and so will attract each other. A normal hydrogen atom would be gravitationally attracted to an anti-hydrogen in exactly the same way that it would be attracted to a normal hydrogen. Dark Energy is unrelated to this concept -- it refers to the accelerated expansion of space itself in the universe.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: If matter attracts matter (gravity), does anti-matter repel matter (anti-matter)?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Sure! Here’s how you could explain it to a 5-year-old:

Imagine you have two kinds of blocks: red blocks and blue blocks. Red blocks like to stick to other red blocks, and blue blocks like to stick to other blue blocks. But when a red block meets a blue block, they push each other away—they don’t like to touch!

In the universe, matter is like the red blocks and anti-matter is like the blue blocks. Matter likes to stick to other matter because of gravity. But if matter meets anti-matter, instead of sticking together, they push each other away in a very big way—they don’t like each other at all!

So, yes—anti-matter and matter don’t just not stick together, they actually push each other away when they meet.
